sources.title: RFC 8289 CoDel
sources.sections_read: Introduction; §3.3 control loop; §5.6 helper control law
sources.confirmed: The design rejects direct classical PID use because queueing violates linear, time-invariant SISO assumptions, and instead motivates a state-space controller and stochastic adaptation. The reasoning determines controller choice and an explicit inverse-square-root drop schedule, so it is a substantive transfer of control principles, not merely a borrowed name.
sources.limits: Out-of-sample IETF counterexample; control engineering versus networking is a domain-boundary judgment, and this single designed counterexample does not estimate frequency in the four sampled families. No implementation was run.

sources.title: PEP 433 parameter naming alternatives
sources.sections_read: Bikeshedding on the name of the new parameter
sources.confirmed: The word sterile is explained using reproductive terminology in a list of possible parameter names. No biological mechanism, structure or performance premise is transferred in this passage.
sources.limits: This term-only observation is not an additional distant-principle gold item and does not establish that metaphors never aid comprehension.

sources.title: Rust RFC 438 alternatives versus unresolved questions
sources.confirmed: The Alternatives section proposes tolerating the grammar inconsistency and disambiguating ad hoc. The nearby None belongs to Unresolved questions, despite a search snippet making an empty-alternatives interpretation tempting.
sources.limits: A search-snippet false positive, not evidence of an empty section or a new accepted case.

sources.title: Rust RFC 1300 actual alternatives
sources.confirmed: The Alternatives section contains coercion through generated function wrappers and doing nothing. None again belongs to Unresolved questions, so this is not an empty-alternatives counterexample.
sources.limits: The exact request timestamp was not saved; the bounded observation window is reported. This reading does not revise corpus membership.

sources.title: Rust RFC 90 missing comparison section
sources.sections_read: All headings and ending after Drawbacks
sources.confirmed: The fixed body has Summary, Motivation, Detailed design and Drawbacks but no independent Alternatives or Prior art section. The preregistered screening ledger excluded it with zero comparison items.
sources.limits: This demonstrates a missing section, not a population rate or proof that no alternatives were considered in review. It is outside the 31 included cases.

sources.title: K265 alternatives section inspection

sources.title: Pre-RFC: Trait for deserializing untrusted input — reviewer-proposed prior art
sources.sections_read: Prior Art and comments2–12; especially reviewer item6 and response8
sources.confirmed: A reviewer supplies the existing Plain Old Data trait; the proposer compares its runtime size/alignment checks and allowed conversion directions with the proposed design. The visible proposal also acknowledges this reference, and other replies challenge whether a library suffices and correct padding/alignment assumptions.
sources.limits: The rendered first post may be edited and no exact edit revision was recovered. This is a noncase review example, not an extra gold item or evidence of final RFC acceptance; usernames and discussion body were not saved.
